description: Gold (LBMA fix) vs the S&P 500 since 1985, both indexed to 100. Over this span gold grew about 13.9× and the S&P (price only) about 43.1×. Interactive chart.
text:
Gold vs the S&P 500
How has gold held up against US stocks? Below, the LBMA gold price and the S&P 500 are both indexed to
100 at the first shared monthly observation (1985-01), with data through 2026-09. Over this sampled span the gold benchmark rose
about
13.9×
and the S&P 500 (price only, excluding dividends) about
43.1×
.
Sources, sampling and calculation methodology
Both indexed to 100 at the start of the overlap.
Gold
= LBMA fix; S&P 500 = price index (excludes dividends). For illustration, not investment advice.
How to read this
Indexing both to 100 makes very different price levels comparable — a value of 400 means the sampled price is four times its starting value. Note the S&P line is
price only
; including reinvested dividends would lift it
further. The gold series excludes dealer premiums, storage, insurance and transaction costs. These are price-index comparisons, not net investor returns.
See also:

,
inflation-adjusted gold
, or

.
